# Twisted Spear · Book II, pp. 542–543
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	542
FACE	front
TH	appendix d: major arcana
P	◇◇ <i>, reach</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	A knobby length of wood, pale as death and hard as steel, tapering to a needle point. The shaft is scored and notched, the tip stained with blood and soot.
P	The Spear is a potent weapon against spirits and demons. They cannot bear its touch and its presence makes them deeply ill at ease.
HR
P	When you <b><i>wield the Twisted Spear as a weapon</i></b>, you ignore magical protections and can harm spirits, demons, and insubstantial creatures.
P	When you <b><i>first plunge the Spear into a spirit or demon</i></b>, your mind reels with strange visions. These tasks become known to you:
C	Impale a foul spirit with the Spear, and keep it skewered until it burns away to nothing.
C	Visit the elder tree from which the Spear was carved, and water its roots with your blood.
C	Face the Pale Hunter and survive the encounter.
C	Spend a fortnight in the wild, eating nothing, naked and unarmed except for the Spear.
C	Pierce your own hand through with the Spear, giving it a shard of your soul and reducing your max HP by 1d4+1.
P	When you <b><i>complete a task</i></b>, mark it off.
P	When you <b><i>have marked 3 tasks</i></b>, you unlock the mysteries of the Twisted Spear. Choose one of the moves on the reverse; you can use that move as long as you wield the Spear. Each time you mark a task thereafter, gain another move from the reverse.

FACE	back
TH	appendix d: major arcana
H3	Mysteries of the Twisted Spear
HR
H2	Moves
HR
C	<b>WHISPERS</b> When you <b><i>grip the shaft of the Twisted Spear</i></b>, you can ask the GM, "What spirits are active here?" and get an honest answer.
HR
C	<b>PROMISE OF DOOM</b> When you <b><i>hold the Twisted Spear and speak aloud an oath to destroy a spirit or demon</i></b>, you do +2d4 damage against them and -4 damage to everything else. This lasts until you destroy them or forsake your oath. If you forsake your oath, mark a consequence.
HR
C	<b>ROOTS OF THE ELDER TREE</b> When you <b><i>stand with your feet firmly on the ground and strike a spirit, ghost, or demon</i></b>, you can mark a consequence to send your target coursing through you and into the depths of the earth, where it is bound fast.
HR
C	<b>DARKNESS LINGERS</b> When you <b><i>strike down a spirit or demon</i></b>, ask the GM for one of its moves and write it down; it is held in the Twisted Spear. When you <b><i>use the stolen move</i></b>, roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, you do it, just like that; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you do it, but choose 1:
B	The move is lost, bleeding away from the Spear
B	Mark a consequence
HR
H2	Consequences
HR
C	Deep beneath the elder tree from which the Spear was carved, something dark and terrible shifts and strains at the roots that bind it.
C	From now on, the first time you Make Camp each session, roll +WIS: <b>on a 10+</b>, your dreams are unpleasant and claustrophobic, but your sleep is restful; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you dream of that which is bound by the elder tree from which the Spear was carved—take disadvantage on your next roll, but ask the GM what you learn; <b>on a 6-</b>, the thing bound by the tree sees you, too. You awake, unrested, and will get no rest this night.
C	You are overwhelmed by a vision of the thing bound by the Spear's tree, its past and its terrible desires.
C	The elder tree from which the Spear was carved shudders and cracks, still whole but wounded and weakened.
C	A lesser evil escapes from the roots of the tree. Ask the GM what is now loose in the world.
C	The tree grows sick and weak, losing its leaves and sprouting only a few in spring.
C	Some natural thing is tainted by the dark power beneath the tree, and goes forth to wreak evil.
C	The tree dies. Its prisoners escape. And the Spear loses all power.
